result.title: Neighbor Crowding Predicts Feature Stability in Sparse Autoencoders
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurReps Workshop (Symmetry and Geometry in Neural Representations), NeurIPS 2026, Proceedings track. 13 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables
result.summary: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) offer an approach to identify language model representations by breaking apart polysemantic features into more sparse, interpretable ones. Yet, it is challenging to identify which of the learned features are actually stable, rather than artifacts of initialization. One approach is to train multiple SAE seeds, and compare the learned features across seeds by cosine similarity, but this is notably costly. This raises the question of whether stable features can be identified without the computational expense of training multiple seeds. In this work, we examine cross-seed feature stability across differing levels of training tokens, and demonstrate that in TopK SAEs, it is highly predictable using six computationally cheap statistics derived from a single training run. Neighbor crowding, a geometric property of the dictionary, is the strongest single predictor, with features that sit in dense regions of the unit sphere more likely to be stable than isolated ones.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 TopK SAE 的跨种子特征稳定性随训练 token 数的变化，发现仅用单次训练的六个廉价统计量即可高度预测稳定性，其中「邻域拥挤」这一字典几何性质是最强单一预测因子：位于单位球密集区域的特征比孤立特征更稳定。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「免多次训练即可判断特征是真信号还是初始化伪影」的统计与几何线索，可能可供核查地迁移到 LVR：用于区分内部状态中真实的视觉/推理内容与训练伪影，并为 latent 相似度比较提供几何解读，但仅在文本 SAE 上验证，需核查其跨模态适用性。
